page: Microsoft Azure D2nlds_v6 is a low-memory, local-disk virtual machine instance from the Dnldv6 family. Built on an x86_64 Intel processor architecture and running on Microsoft Hyper-V, this configuration provides 2 dedicated virtual CPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance includes 118 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local scratch storage and supports Premium Storage configurations, but it does not bundle dedicated GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The 1:2 processor-to-memory ratio positions the D2nlds_v6 away from memory-heavy applications and toward workloads focused on direct processing capacity and local disk caching. By allocating less RAM per core than standard general-purpose profiles, the hardware avoids excess memory overhead, serving environments that require dedicated compute cycles without high memory allocation footprints.

Integrated NVMe SSD storage provides low-latency local disk access for transient data, temporary caches, and rapid read/write scratch space, reducing dependency on external network storage for short-term files. The limitation to 4.0 GB total RAM constitutes a tradeoff for memory-intensive jobs, bounding its scope to small-footprint workloads such as web serving, microservices, continuous integration agents, and compute tasks requiring direct fast scratch space.

The system is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs, 4.0 GB of RAM, and 118 GB of onboard NVMe SSD local storage. Operating with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this configuration represents a low-memory variant optimized for cost-effective computing where extensive RAM is unnecessary. It does not include hardware accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, but it is capable of interfacing with Premium Storage. The local NVMe SSD provides rapid, low-latency scratch storage, making this instance suitable for edge processing nodes, stateless application layers, CI/CD runners, and lightweight proxy or web serving workloads that benefit from fast local caching without expansive memory overhead.
